title: Where Do Numbers Live?
objective: Numbers have a location relative to each other — they can be placed in order along a path, and that placement itself carries meaning.
newIdea: Number location — the seed of the number line, used from here through algebra.

teaching.setup: A blank path with a start point (zero) marked.
teaching.see: If this end is zero, where do you think 3 belongs?
teaching.break: Place a few numbers (0, 1, 2, 3) one at a time, checking each against more than the last one, so further along.
teaching.build: Fill in a short run of consecutive numbers on the path.
teaching.transform: The same numbers, shown as a path of positions instead of separate counted groups.

check.prompt: Does the order along the path match: more is farther from zero?

examples.second: Inserting 6 and 7 onto an already-placed 0-5 path.
examples.transfer: Given two already-placed numbers (e.g. 2 and 6), predict roughly where 4 belongs between them.

mastery.evidence: Correctly places 4-5 given numbers in order along a path and justifies more is farther along.
